mechanism_evidence.claim: When StreamWindowManager reports fullscreen, StreamPage recalculates displayInfo, pan/zoom parent size, and XComponent size from updateScreenSize/calculateXComponentSize rather than the actual drawable window viewport.
The correct viewport-owned path exists only in the non-fullscreen branch, where getCurrentWindowViewportSize feeds calculateXComponentSizeForViewport and panZoomHandler.setParentSize.

The isFullscreen ownership is a local flag toggled only by the app's manual window-mode transition; a system PiP transition can leave this flag true while the drawable viewport is no longer the full display.
The fullscreen sizing path reads display.getDefaultDisplaySync width and height, so in PiP it can size the XComponent to the device display instead of the visible PiP drawable area.
The window manager has an API that reads windowRect/drawableRect and converts it to vp, which is the viewport needed for PiP/free-window sizing.

observations.summary: The sizing owner is split between StreamPage.recalculateXComponentSize and StreamWindowManager. PiP changes the visible drawable viewport, but the app can still consider itself fullscreen, so StreamPage takes the fullscreen branch and StreamWindowManager.calculateXComponentSize sizes from the default display. That makes the centered landscape surface larger than the PiP viewport and clipped; the same stale screen dimensions are also passed to PanZoomHandler as its parent size, allowing touch inverse mapping and bounds to drift after the viewport change.

mechanism_evidence.claim: The default XComponent sizing owner derives video fit from display.getDefaultDisplaySync screen pixel dimensions, not the current window or PiP viewport, so a landscape stream can be sized for the full display and then clipped by the smaller PiP container.

The page updates xComponentWidth, xComponentHeight, displayInfo, and PanZoom parent size during viewport changes; if this path uses full-screen sizing or stale screen dimensions during PiP/window transitions, the visible area clips the centered surface and touch mapping remains based on the wrong parent size.

PanZoom stores parentWidth and parentHeight and constrains zoom translation from those dimensions, so stale full-screen dimensions after a PiP viewport change directly explain drift in zoom touch mapping.

observations.summary: The root ownership is StreamWindowManager's XComponent sizing.
